title: You feel like you’re running on empty… but heaven says, you’re not done yet.
paragraphs: You feel like you’re running on empty… but heaven says, you’re not done yet.

“But those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength;
they shall mount up with wings like eagles,
they shall run and not be weary,
they shall walk and not faint.” — Isaiah 40:31
Pause there.

Not those who hustle harder.
Not those who fake strength.
Those who wait.

That word cuts deep.
Because waiting feels like losing.
Like delay.
Like silence from God.
But here’s what we miss…

Waiting on the Lord is not passive.
It’s positioning.

It’s saying,
“God, I don’t have the strength—but You do.”
And that’s where grace walks in.

God doesn’t just repair your strength.
He renews it.
Fresh.
Heaven-breathed.
Stronger than what you had before the breaking.

You thought you were grounded—
but God says, you will fly.

You thought you’d collapse—
but God says, you will run.

You thought you’d quit—
but God says, you will walk and not faint.
Not because you’re strong.

But because Jesus carried your weakness to the cross—
and rose again with power you could never earn.

This promise is not for the perfect.
It’s for the dependent.

So if you’re tired… good.
You’re exactly where grace begins.

Wait on Him.
Trust Him.
Lean all the weight of your soul on Christ.
And watch what happens next.
Strength will come.
From exhaustion to elevation—because Jesus renews what the world drains.
